cues.en: A lot of you have asked me to do a video about the delayed choice quantum eraser, an experiment that supposedly rewrites the past. I haven't done that simply because there are already lots of videos about it. For example, Matt from PBS Space Time, the always amazing Joe Scott, and recently also Don Lincoln from Fermilab.
cues.zh: 你们很多人都让我做一期关于延迟选择量子擦除器的视频，这个实验据说能改写过去。我一直没做，纯粹是因为相关的视频已经很多了。比如 PBS Space Time 的 Matt，一向惊艳的 Joe Scott，最近还有 Fermilab 的 Don Lincoln。

cues.en: And how many videos do you really need about the same thing if that thing isn't a kitten in a box?
cues.zh: 而且，如果那东西不是盒子里的猫咪，同一件事你到底还需要多少个视频呢？

cues.en: However, having watched all those gentlemen's videos about quantum erasing,
cues.zh: 不过，看完那些先生们关于量子擦除的所有视频之后，

cues.en: I think they're all wrong.
cues.zh: 我觉得他们全都错了。

cues.en: The quantum eraser isn't remotely as weird as you think, doesn't actually erase anything,
cues.zh: 量子擦除器根本没有你想的那么诡异，它其实什么都没擦除，

cues.en: and certainly doesn't rewrite the past.
cues.zh: 更不会改写过去。

cues.en: And that's what we'll talk about today.
cues.zh: 这就是我们今天要讲的内容。

cues.en: Let's start with a puzzle that has nothing to do with quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 我们先从一个与量子力学毫无关系的谜题开始。

cues.en: Peter's 46 years old, and he's captain of a container ship.
cues.zh: Peter 46 岁，是一艘集装箱船的船长。

cues.en: He ships goods between two places that are 100 kilometers apart.
cues.zh: 他在相距 100 公里的两个地方之间运送货物。

cues.en: Let's call them A and B.
cues.zh: 我们称它们为 A 和 B。

cues.en: He starts his round trip at A with the ship only half full.
cues.zh: 他从 A 开始这趟往返航行，船里只装了一半。

cues.en: Three quarters of the way to B, he adds more containers to fill the ship, which slows him down by a factor of two.
cues.zh: 在去 B 的四分之三路程处，他又装上更多集装箱把船填满，这让他的速度降为原来的一半。

cues.en: On the return trip, his ship is empty. How old is the captain?
cues.zh: 返程时，他的船是空的。船长多大年纪？

cues.en: If you don't know the answer, let's rewind this question to the beginning.
cues.zh: 如果你不知道答案，我们把这个问题倒回到开头。

cues.en: Years old and he's captain of a container ship. Peter's 46 years old.
cues.zh: 他 46 岁，是一艘集装箱船的船长。Peter 46 岁。

cues.en: The answer's right there.
cues.zh: 答案就在那儿。

cues.en: Everything I told you after that was completely unnecessary and just there to confuse you.
cues.zh: 在那之后我讲的一切都完全没必要，纯粹是为了迷惑你。

cues.en: The quantum eraser is a puzzle just like this. The quantum eraser is an experiment that combines two quantum effects, interference and entanglement.
cues.zh: 量子擦除器就是这样一个谜题。量子擦除器是一个结合了两种量子效应的实验：干涉和纠缠。

cues.en: Interference of quantum particles can itself be tested by the double slit experiment.
cues.zh: 量子粒子的干涉本身就可以用双缝实验来检验。

cues.en: For the double slit experiment,
cues.zh: 在双缝实验中，

cues.en: you shoot a coherent beam of particles at a plate with two thin openings.
cues.zh: 你向一块带有两条细缝的板发射一束相干粒子束。

cues.en: That's the double slit.
cues.zh: 这就是双缝。

cues.en: On the screen behind it, you then observe several lines, usually five or seven, but not two.
cues.zh: 在它后面的屏幕上，你会看到若干条纹，通常是五条或七条，而不是两条。

cues.en: This is an interference pattern created by overlapping waves.
cues.zh: 这是由波叠加形成的干涉图样。

cues.en: When a crest meets a trough, the waves cancel and that makes a dark spot on the screen.
cues.zh: 当波峰遇到波谷时，波会相互抵消，在屏幕上形成暗点。

cues.en: When crest meets crest, they add up and that makes a bright spot. The amazing thing about the double slit is that you get this pattern even if you let only one particle at a time pass through the slits.
cues.zh: 当波峰遇到波峰时，它们会叠加，形成亮点。双缝的神奇之处在于，即使每次只让一个粒子通过狭缝，你也会得到这种图样。

cues.en: This means that even single particles act like waves.
cues.zh: 这意味着，单个粒子也会表现得像波。

cues.en: We therefore describe quantum particles with a wave function usually denoted Psi.
cues.zh: 因此我们用波函数描述量子粒子，通常记作 Psi。

cues.en: The interesting thing about the double slit experiment is that if you measure which slit the particles go through,
cues.zh: 双缝实验有趣的地方在于，如果你测量粒子穿过哪条缝，

cues.en: the interference pattern disappears.
cues.zh: 干涉图样就会消失。

cues.en: Instead,
cues.zh: 相反，

cues.en: the particles behave like particles again, and you get two blobs,
cues.zh: 粒子又会表现得像粒子，你会得到两个斑块，

cues.en: one from each of the slits.
cues.zh: 分别来自两条缝。

cues.en: Well, actually you don't.
cues.zh: 嗯，其实你并不会。

cues.en: Though you've almost certainly seen that elsewhere.
cues.zh: 你几乎肯定在别处见过这个。

cues.en: Just because you know which slit the wave function goes through,
cues.zh: 仅仅因为你知道波函数穿过的是哪条狭缝，

cues.en: doesn't mean it stops being a wave function.
cues.zh: 并不意味着它就不再是波函数了。

cues.en: It's just no longer a wave function going through two slits.
cues.zh: 它只是不再是一个穿过两条狭缝的波函数。

cues.en: It's now a wave function going through only one slit. So you get a one slit diffraction pattern.
cues.zh: 现在它是一个只穿过一条狭缝的波函数。于是你会得到单缝衍射图样。

cues.en: Was that?
cues.zh: 那是什么？

cues.en: That's also an interference pattern, but a fuzzier one, and indeed looks mostly like a blob,
cues.zh: 那也是一种干涉图样，只是更模糊，而且看起来主要像一团斑块，

cues.en: but a very blurry blob.
cues.zh: 但是一团非常模糊的斑块。

cues.en: And if you add the blobs from the two individual slits,
cues.zh: 如果你把两个单缝各自产生的光斑相加，

cues.en: they'll overlap and still pretty much look like one blob.
cues.zh: 它们会重叠，看起来仍然基本就是一个光斑。

cues.en: Not, as you see in many videos, two cleanly separated ones.
cues.zh: 而不是像你在很多视频里看到的那样，两个清晰分开的光斑。

cues.en: You may think this is nitpicking,
cues.zh: 你可能觉得这是吹毛求疵，

cues.en: but it'll be relevant to understanding the quantum eraser, so keep this in mind.
cues.zh: 但这对理解量子擦除器很关键，所以请记住这一点。

cues.en: It's not so relevant for the double slit experiment, because regardless of whether you think it's one blob or two, the sum of the images from both separate slits is not the image you get from both slits together.
cues.zh: 这对双缝实验倒没那么关键，因为不管你认为它是一个光斑还是两个光斑，两个单缝图像之和都不是双缝同时打开时得到的图像。

cues.en: The double slit experiment therefore shows that in quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 因此，双缝实验表明，在量子力学中，

cues.en: the result of a measurement depends
cues.zh: 测量结果取决于

cues.en: on what you measure.
cues.zh: 你测量的是什么。

cues.en: Yes, that's weird.
cues.zh: 是的，这很奇怪。

cues.en: The other ingredient that you need for the quantum eraser is entanglement.
cues.zh: 量子擦除器需要的另一个要素是纠缠。

cues.en: I've talked about entanglement several times previously,
cues.zh: 我之前已经谈过好几次纠缠了，

cues.en: so let me just briefly remind you: entangled particles share some information,
cues.zh: 所以让我简单提醒你：纠缠粒子共享一些信息，

cues.en: but you don't know which particle has which share until you measure it.
cues.zh: 但在测量之前，你不知道哪个粒子拥有哪部分信息。

cues.en: It could be, for example, that you know the particles have a total spin of zero,
cues.zh: 例如，可能是你知道这些粒子的总自旋为零，

cues.en: but you don't know the spin of each individual particle.
cues.zh: 但你不知道每个粒子的自旋。

cues.en: Antenna particles are handy because they allow you to measure quantum effects over large distances,
cues.zh: 天线粒子很好用，因为它们让你能在远距离上测量量子效应，

cues.en: which makes them super extra weird.
cues.zh: 这也让它们格外诡异。

cues.en: Okay, now to the quantum eraser.
cues.zh: 好，现在来说量子擦除器。

cues.en: You take your beam of particles,
cues.zh: 你拿一束粒子，

cues.en: usually photons, and direct it at the double slit.
cues.zh: 通常是光子，把它对准双缝。

cues.en: After the double slit, you place a crystal that converts each single photon into a pair of antenna photons.
cues.zh: 在双缝之后放一块晶体，把每个单光子转换成一对天线光子。

cues.en: From each pair, you take one and direct it onto a screen.
cues.zh: 从每一对中取出一个，把它引导到一个屏幕上。

cues.en: There, you measure whether they interfere.
cues.zh: 在那里，测量它们是否发生干涉。

cues.en: I have drawn the photons which come from the two different places in the crystal with two different colors,
cues.zh: 我把来自晶体中两个不同位置的光子画成了两种不同颜色，

cues.en: but this is just so it's easier to see what's going on. These photons actually have the same color. If you create these entangled pairs after the double slit,
cues.zh: 但这只是为了更容易看清发生了什么。这些光子实际上颜色相同。如果你在双缝之后产生这些纠缠光子对，

cues.en: then the wave function of the photon depends on which slit the photons went through.
cues.zh: 那么光子的波函数就取决于这些光子穿过了哪条缝。

cues.en: This information
cues.zh: 这些信息

cues.en: comes from the location where the pairs were created, and is usually called the which way information.
cues.zh: 来自光子对产生的位置，通常被称为“哪条路径”信息。

cues.en: Because of this which way information,
cues.zh: 由于这个“哪条路径”信息，

cues.en: the photons on the screen can't create an interference pattern.
cues.zh: 屏幕上的光子无法形成干涉图案。

cues.en: What's with the other side of the entangled particles?
cues.zh: 那纠缠粒子的另一侧呢？

cues.en: That's where things get tricky.
cues.zh: 这里就变得棘手了。

cues.en: On the other side, you measure the particles in two different ways.
cues.zh: 在另一侧，你用两种不同的方式测量粒子。

cues.en: In the first case, you measure the which way information directly, so you have two detectors, let's call them d one and d two.
cues.zh: 第一种情况，你直接测量“哪条路径”信息，所以你有两个探测器，我们称它们为 d one 和 d two。

cues.en: The first detector is on the path of the photons from the left slit,
cues.zh: 第一个探测器位于来自左缝的光子路径上，

cues.en: the second detector is on the path of the photons from the right slit.
cues.zh: 第二个探测器位于来自右缝的光子路径上。

cues.en: If you measure the photons with detectors d one and d two, you see no interference pattern. But alternatively,
cues.zh: 如果用探测器d1和d2测量光子，你不会看到干涉图案。但另一种方式是，

cues.en: you can turn off the first two detectors and instead combine the two beams in two different ways.
cues.zh: 你可以关闭前两个探测器，转而以两种不同方式合并两束光。

cues.en: These two white bars are mirrors and just redirect the beam.
cues.zh: 这两条白色条状物是镜子，只是改变光束的方向。

cues.en: The semi transparent one is a beam splitter.
cues.zh: 半透明的那块是分束器。

cues.en: This means half of the photons go through and the other half is reflected.
cues.zh: 这意味着有一半光子穿过，另一半被反射。

cues.en: This looks a little confusing,
cues.zh: 这看起来有点让人困惑，

cues.en: but the point is just that you combine the two beams so that you no longer know which way the photon came.
cues.zh: 但关键只是把两束光合并起来，让你不再知道光子是从哪条路来的。

cues.en: This is the erasure of the which way information.
cues.zh: 这就是擦除“路径”信息。

cues.en: And then you measure those combined beams in detectors D three and D four.
cues.zh: 然后在探测器 D3 和 D4 中测量这些合并后的光束。

cues.en: A measurement on one of those two detectors does not tell you which slit the photon went through. Finally,
cues.zh: 对这两个探测器之一的测量，并不能告诉你光子穿过了哪条缝。最后，

cues.en: you measure the distribution of photons on the screen
cues.zh: 你测量屏幕上光子的分布

cues.en: that are internal partners of those photons that went to d three.
cues.zh: 这些光子是那些前往 D3 的光子的内部伙伴。

cues.en: These photons create an interference pattern.
cues.zh: 这些光子会形成干涉图案。

cues.en: You can alternatively
cues.zh: 另一种做法是

cues.en: measure the distribution of photons on the screen that are partner particles of those photons that went to d four.
cues.zh: 测量屏幕上光子的分布，这些光子是与前往 D4 的光子配对的粒子。

cues.en: Those will also create an interference pattern.
cues.zh: 它们也会形成干涉图案。

cues.en: This is the quantum erasure.
cues.zh: 这就是量子擦除。

cues.en: It seems you've managed to get rid of the which way information by combining those paths,
cues.zh: 看起来，你通过合并这些路径，成功去掉了“哪条路”信息，

cues.en: and that restores the interference pattern.
cues.zh: 从而恢复了干涉图案。

cues.en: In the delayed choice quantum eraser experiment,
cues.zh: 在延迟选择量子擦除实验中，

cues.en: the erasure happens well after the entangled partner particle hit the screen.
cues.zh: 擦除发生在纠缠配对粒子击中屏幕很久之后。

cues.en: This is fairly easy to do just by making the path of those photons long enough. If you watch the other videos about this experiment on YouTube,
cues.zh: 只要把那些光子的路径拉得足够长，这就相当容易做到。如果你看过 YouTube 上关于这个实验的其他视频，

cues.en: they'll now go on to explain that this seems to imply
cues.zh: 这些视频接下来会解释说，这似乎意味着

cues.en: that the choice of what you measure on the one side of the experiment
cues.zh: 在实验的一侧选择测量什么，

cues.en: decides what happened on the other side BEFORE you even made that choice.
cues.zh: 会决定另一侧在你做出那个选择之前发生了什么。

cues.en: Because the photons must have known whether to interfere or not before you decided whether to erase the which way information.
cues.zh: 因为在你决定是否擦除路径信息之前，光子就一定已经知道自己该不该干涉了。

cues.en: But this is clearly nonsense.
cues.zh: 但这显然说不通。

cues.en: Because let's rewind this explanation to the beginning.
cues.zh: 因为让我们把这个解释倒回开头。

cues.en: Because of this which way information, the photons on the screen can't create an interference pattern.
cues.zh: 由于这个“哪条路”信息，屏幕上的光子无法形成干涉图案。

cues.en: The photons on the screen can't create an interference pattern.
cues.zh: 屏幕上的光子无法形成干涉图案。

cues.en: Everything I told you after this is completely irrelevant.
cues.zh: 我在这之后讲的所有内容都完全不相关了。

cues.en: It doesn't matter at all what you do on the other side of the experiment.
cues.zh: 你在实验另一端做什么都完全无关紧要。

cues.en: The photons on the screen will always create the same pattern.
cues.zh: 屏幕上的光子总会形成相同的图案。

cues.en: And it'll never be an interference pattern.
cues.zh: 它永远不会形成干涉图样。

cues.en: Wait, didn't I just tell you that you do get an interference pattern if you use detectors D3 and D4?
cues.zh: 等等，我刚才不是告诉过你，如果用探测器D3和D4，确实会得到干涉图样吗？

cues.en: Indeed.
cues.zh: 确实如此。

cues.en: But I've omitted a crucial part of the information which is missing in all those other YouTube videos.
cues.zh: 但我省略了一个关键信息，而这个信息在那些其他YouTube视频里都缺失了。

cues.en: It's that those interference patterns
cues.zh: 那就是这些干涉图样

cues.en: are not the same.
cues.zh: 并不相同。

cues.en: And if you add them, you get exactly the same as you get from detectors one and two,
cues.zh: 而如果你把它们叠加起来，得到的结果和从探测器1和2得到的一模一样，

cues.en: namely these two overlapping blurry blobs.
cues.zh: 也就是这两个相互重叠的模糊光斑。

cues.en: This is why it matters that you know the combined pattern of two single slits doesn't give you two separate blobs as they normally show you. What you actually do in the eraser experiment
cues.zh: 这就是为什么你要知道：两个单缝的合并图样，并不像通常展示的那样会给出两个分离的斑块。在擦除实验中，你实际做的是

cues.en: is that you sample the photon pairs in two groups.
cues.zh: 就是把光子对分成两组进行采样。

cues.en: And you do that in two different ways.
cues.zh: 而且你用两种不同的方式来做。

cues.en: If you use detector one and two, you sample them so that the entangled partners on the screen do not create an interference pattern for each detector separately.
cues.zh: 如果你使用探测器1和2，你采样它们的方式会使得屏幕上的纠缠伙伴不会为每个探测器分别产生干涉图样。

cues.en: If you use detector three and four, they each separately create an interference pattern,
cues.zh: 如果你使用探测器三和四，它们各自会单独产生干涉图样，

cues.en: but together they don't.
cues.zh: 但放在一起就不会。

cues.en: This means that the interference pattern really comes from selectively
cues.zh: 这意味着干涉图样其实来自选择性地

cues.en: disregarding
cues.zh: 忽略

cues.en: some of the particles.
cues.zh: 一部分粒子。

cues.en: That this is possible has nothing to do with quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 这件事之所以可能，与量子力学毫无关系。

cues.en: I could throw coins on the floor and then later decide to disregard some of those and create any kind of pattern.
cues.zh: 我可以把硬币扔到地上，然后之后再决定忽略其中一些，并造出任意图案。

cues.en: Clearly,
cues.zh: 显然，

cues.en: this doesn't rewrite the past.
cues.zh: 这并不会改写过去。

cues.en: This, by the way, has nothing to do with the particular realization of the quantum eraser experiment that I've discussed.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这与我之前讨论的量子擦除实验的具体实现方式无关。

cues.en: This experiment
cues.zh: 这个实验

cues.en: has been done in a number of different ways,
cues.zh: 已经用多种不同的方式做过，

cues.en: but what I just told you is generally true.
cues.zh: 但我刚才告诉你的内容普遍成立。

cues.en: These interference patterns will always combine to give the original non interference pattern. This is not to say that there's nothing weird going on in this experiment.
cues.zh: 这些干涉图样总会叠加成原本的非干涉图样。这并不是说这个实验里没有奇怪之处。

cues.en: But what's weird about it is the same thing that weird already about the normal double slit experiment.
cues.zh: 但它的奇怪之处，与普通双缝实验里本来就有的奇怪之处是同一回事。

cues.en: Namely,
cues.zh: 也就是说，

cues.en: if you look at the wavefunction of a single particle,
cues.zh: 如果你看单个粒子的波函数，

cues.en: then that distributes in space.
cues.zh: 那么它会在空间中分布。

cues.en: Yet, when you measure it, the particle is suddenly in one particular place,
cues.zh: 然而，当你测量它时，粒子会突然出现在某个特定位置，

cues.en: and the result must be correlated throughout space and fit to the measurement setting.
cues.zh: 而且结果必须在整个空间中相互关联，并与测量设置相匹配。

cues.en: I actually think the BOM experiment is far weirder than the quantum eraser.
cues.zh: 我其实觉得 BOM 实验比量子擦除实验怪得多。

cues.en: Check out my earlier video for more on that. When I was working on this video, I thought,
cues.zh: 想了解更多，可以看看我之前的视频。我在做这个视频时想，

cues.en: certainly someone must have explained this before.
cues.zh: 肯定有人之前解释过这个。

cues.en: But the only person I could find who'd done that is Sean Carroll in a blog post two years ago.
cues.zh: 但我能找到的唯一做过这件事的人，是 Sean Carroll，他在两年前的一篇博客文章里做过。

cues.en: Yes, you can trust Jean with the quantum stuff.
